title: Firefox MV3 CSP token vocabulary, measured in real extension contexts

browser.name: Mozilla Firefox
browser.driver: web-ext 8.3.0, temporary add-on into a throwaway profile
browser.note: Same Firefox version (155.0.1) as the workstation-2 cell in W1-S02a, so the cells are comparable.

prefs: extensions.originControls.grantByDefault=true  (reporting only - Firefox MV3 gates host_permissions behind origin controls)

wasm_fixture.note: INLINE in the probe, not fetched, so the CSP question is isolated from Firefox host_permissions gating.

liveness: An /alive tab beacon proves the event page executed. 'The extension did not load' and 'it loaded and the token blocked everything' are different results and must not be inferred from one another.

machine_changes.SOURCE: winget Mozilla.Firefox (installer hash verified by winget)
machine_changes.REASON: S-02a-2a-2 requires real Firefox; workstation 1 had none. No Firefox result may be inferred from Chrome.
machine_changes.IMPACT: System-wide install under C:\Program Files\Mozilla Firefox. Not set as default browser.

machine_changes.REASON: Install a temporary MV3 add-on into a throwaway Firefox profile; the same tool the existing W1-S02a-2 harness uses.
machine_changes.IMPACT: node_modules inside this experiment's harness only; gitignored.

known_limitations: Windows only. Firefox on Linux is a separate cell (S-02a-1, still UNKNOWN).

Payload field 'reportedVia' is always null: it is assigned after the payload is serialised. The collector's own '__via' tag carries the truth - all 24 reports arrived via fetch. Cosmetic; affects no finding.
